q.t: Choose the pronoun: Aman is tall. ___ plays basketball.
q.e: Aman is the subject of ‘plays’, so use the subject form ‘He’.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: The teacher praised ___. (Riya)
q.e: Riya receives the praise (object), so use ‘her’.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: This book is ___. (it belongs to me)
q.e: Standing alone at the end, use ‘mine’. ‘my’ needs a noun after it (my book).

q.t: Choose the pronoun: The cat licked ___ paw.
q.e: Belonging ‘its’ has no apostrophe. ‘it's’ means ‘it is’.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: We cleaned the room ___.
q.e: ‘we’ matches ‘ourselves’ (plural, -selves).

q.t: Which word is a demonstrative pronoun? That is my school.
q.e: ‘That’ points to the school and stands in for it.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: ___ is knocking at the door?
q.e: Asking about a person who is the subject (doing the knocking) → ‘Who’.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: Rohan and Sara are here. I can see ___.
q.e: They are being seen (object), so use ‘them’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe. ‘you're’ means ‘you are’.

q.t: Choose the pronoun: The girls did their homework by ___.
q.e: ‘girls’ is plural → themselves. ‘theirselves’ is not a word.

q.t: Choose the correct option: Riya and ___ went to the market.
q.e: Cover ‘Riya and’: ‘I went to the market’ ✓, ‘me went’ ✗. It is the subject.

q.t: Choose the correct option: Mother gave sweets to Ravi and ___.
q.e: Cover ‘Ravi and’: ‘gave sweets to me’ ✓. After the preposition ‘to’, use the object form.

q.t: Choose the correct option: This secret is between you and ___.
q.e: ‘between’ is a preposition and takes the object form: between you and me.

q.t: Choose the relative pronoun: This is the boy ___ broke the window.
q.e: For a person who is the subject of ‘broke’, use ‘who’.

q.t: Choose the relative pronoun: The dog ___ bit me was caught.
q.e: For an animal or thing, use ‘which’ (or ‘that’).

q.t: Choose the relative pronoun: That is the girl ___ father is a pilot.
q.e: ‘whose’ shows belonging — the girl’s father.

q.t: Is himself reflexive or emphatic in The king himself came to see us.?
q.e: Remove it: ‘The king came to see us’ still works. It only adds force → emphatic.

q.t: Is herself reflexive or emphatic in She cut herself with a knife.?
q.e: Remove it: ‘She cut with a knife’ breaks. The action turns back on the subject → reflexive.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: You, he and I will go.
I, you and he will go.
He, I and you will go.
I, he and you will go.
q.e: Polite order: 2nd person (you), 3rd person (he), then yourself (I) last.

q.t: Which is an indefinite pronoun?
q.e: ‘somebody’ does not point to one particular person — it is indefinite.

q.t: Choose the correct option: ___ did you invite to the party?
q.e: Answer it: ‘I invited him.’ ‘him’ is the object, so use ‘whom’.

q.t: Choose the correct option: The man ___ you met is my uncle.
q.e: ‘you met him’ — the man is the object of ‘met’, so ‘whom’ (‘that’ is also fine).

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is taller than me am.
q.e: Finish the hidden thought: ‘taller than I (am)’. In formal English the subject form ‘I’ is used. (‘than me’ is common in speech.)

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Please call Ravi or me if you need help.
Please call Ravi or myself if you need help.
Please call Ravi or I if you need help.
Please call Ravi or mine if you need help.
q.e: Cover ‘Ravi or’: ‘call me’. ‘myself’ is only for reflexive or emphatic use, not a polite ‘me’.

q.t: Choose the correct option: Each of the boys must bring ___ own lunch.
q.e: ‘Each’ means every single one, so the pronoun is singular: his. (‘their’ is now accepted in speech, but school grammar expects ‘his’.)

q.t: Choose the correct option: Neither of the girls has finished ___ work.
q.e: ‘Neither’ = not this one and not that one — one at a time, so singular: her.

q.t: Which word is a pronoun here? This is the house that Jack built.
q.e: ‘This’ stands in for a noun (demonstrative) and ‘that’ refers back to ‘house’ and joins the clause (relative).

q.t: Find the error: The players hurt theirselves during practice.
q.e: ‘theirselves’ is not a word. The plural reflexive for ‘they’ is ‘themselves’.

q.t: Choose the correct option: These books are ___, not ours.
q.e: Standing alone (no noun after it) and parallel to ‘ours’ → theirs, with no apostrophe.

q.t: Choose the correct option: It was ___ who called you.
q.e: Formal grammar uses the subject form after ‘it was’: ‘It was she (who called)’. She did the calling.

q.t: Choose the correct option: The prize was shared between Meena and ___.
q.e: After the preposition ‘between’, use object forms: between Meena and him.

q.t: Choose the correct option: ___ do you think will win the match?
q.e: Remove ‘do you think’: ‘Who will win?’ — it is the subject of ‘will win’, so ‘who’, not ‘whom’.

q.t: Choose the correct option: The student ___ the principal praised is my cousin.
q.e: ‘the principal praised him’ — the student is the object of ‘praised’, so ‘whom’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Everyone has done his or her best.
q.e: ‘Everyone’ is singular (has), and the matching pronoun is ‘his or her’ in formal grammar.

q.t: Find the error: Let you and I finish this before lunch.
q.e: ‘Let’ is a verb and takes the object: ‘Let me’, so ‘Let you and me’. Cover ‘you and’ to check.

q.t: Choose the correct option: He is the only one of the students who ___ passed.
q.e: ‘who’ refers to ‘the only one’ (singular), so the verb is singular: has.

q.t: Choose the correct option: I enjoy ___ when I'm on holiday.
q.e: ‘enjoy’ needs an object; when the subject enjoys, the object turns back on the subject → reflexive ‘myself’.

q.t: Which sentence uses ‘that’ as a relative pronoun?
o: The film that we saw was scary.
q.e: Here ‘that’ joins a clause (we saw) and refers back to ‘film’. In the others ‘that’ points (demonstrative).

q.t: Choose the correct option: Neither you nor I ___ to blame.
q.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: ‘I am’.

q.t: Choose the correct option: Whose is this umbrella? — It is ___.
q.e: The answer names the owner: one person, Rina → Rina's (a possessive noun standing for ‘Rina's umbrella’).
